question: Where can I get a list of thermal and nuclear power plants in the United States, with location, fuel or technology, capacity (MW), operator, status and annual generation?

answer.summary: EIA's Form EIA-860 (final 2025 data, released 2026-09-10) is the national generator-level table: plant coordinates, technology and fuel, nameplate and net MW, status and operator. Tested: 11,194 fossil and nuclear generators at 3,128 plants (96 nuclear units at 56 plants). EIA-860M (September 2026) updates status monthly, including planned and retired units. EIA-923 gives 2025 net generation in MWh by plant, prime mover and fuel, nuclear by unit. All join on plant code; Vogtle (649) and Scherer (6257) were cross-checked. NRC pages blocked scripted access.
main_caveats: Counting units differ: EIA-860 is per generator (27,919 operable), EIA-923 per plant x prime mover x fuel (nuclear by unit), so MWh do not map one to one to generators.
Capacity bases differ (nameplate vs net summer/winter MW); EIA-923 reports net generation only, no gross column seen.
Operator is the day-to-day operator (Utility ID); owners appear only in Schedule 4 for joint or third-party ownership.
EIA-860M capacities are preliminary and corrected silently; latest published file was September 2026 (October-December names redirect).
No thermal-only table exists: 11,194 generators / 3,128 plants come from my Technology filter (fossil + nuclear; biomass, waste, geothermal excluded).
NRC reactor pages refused scripted access (403); licensee and thermal-power data from NRC were not tested.
answer.confidence_reason: EIA-860, 860M and 923 files were downloaded, parsed and cross-checked on two plants; the thermal subset is my technology filter and NRC pages were unreachable.

attributes.note: Plant latitude/longitude in the EIA-860 Plant sheet for all 3,128 fossil/nuclear plants; generators share the plant point.
Technology, prime mover and up to six energy-source codes per generator; multi-fuel details in the MultiFuel file.
Nameplate, net summer and net winter MW per generator (Vogtle unit 1: 1,215 / 1,150 / 1,150).
Utility ID/Name is the company running the generator day to day; owners only in Schedule 4 (Vogtle has four owners).
OP/SB/OA/OS per generator in EIA-860; EIA-860M adds planned (P, L, T, U, V), retired and canceled inventories.
2025 net generation in MWh by plant x prime mover x fuel, nuclear by unit; Page 4 by generator; no gross figure seen.

sources.name: Annual Electric Generator Report, Form EIA-860 (detailed data)
sources.format: Zip of Excel (.xlsx) workbooks: Utility, Plant, Generator (Operable/Proposed/Retired and Canceled), Wind, Solar, Energy Storage, Multifuel, Owner, environmental files; Layout and instructions
sources.summary: EIA's annual generator survey: every generator at plants of 1 MW or more with plant coordinates, technology and fuel, nameplate and net MW, status and operator. Tested: 11,194 fossil and nuclear generators at 3,128 plants.
sources.coverage_note: Final 2025 data (released 2026-09-10); retired tab is not comprehensive; no thermal-only table.
caveats: Generator is the counting unit; coordinates are per plant.
Utility is the operator; owners are in Schedule 4 for shared ownership only.

problems: The early-release file eia8602025ER.zip answered with a 301 redirect to /cneaf/electricity/ followed by a 503: not available.

records_total is the Operable generator tab (Proposed 2,851; Retired and Canceled 5,806; Plant sheet 17,349 plants); records_for_country is fossil+nuclear operable generators. Researcher filter used for counts: Technology in Nuclear, Conventional Steam Coal, Natural Gas Steam Turbine, Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle, Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine, Natural Gas Internal Combustion Engine, Petroleum Liquids, Petroleum Coke, Other Gases, Other Natural Gas, Coal Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle.

example.example_request: curl -L -o eia8602025.zip https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860/xls/eia8602025.zip && unzip eia8602025.zip -d eia860_2025  # then join 2___Plant_Y2025.xlsx and 3_1_Generator_Y2025.xlsx (sheet Operable) on Plant Code (e.g. 649)
example.example_result: Plant Code 649 Vogtle, operator Georgia Power Co (Utility ID 7140), Burke GA, 33.1427 / -81.7625; generators 1-4 Nuclear ST, nameplate 1215/1215/1114/1114 MW, status OP.

sources.name: Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory (Form EIA-860M)
sources.format: Excel (.xlsx) workbook per month with sheets Operating, Planned, Retired, Canceled or Postponed and Puerto Rico variants
sources.summary: Monthly EIA update of the generator inventory (operating, planned, retired, canceled) with planned-project status codes; September 2026 file lists 11,258 fossil and nuclear operating generators.
sources.coverage_note: Latest published inventory is September 2026 (released 2026-10-23); capacities are preliminary.
caveats: Future-month file names on the page redirect (301).
Operating sheet lacks coordinates; use EIA-860 Plant.

problems: october_generator2026.xlsx, november_generator2026.xlsx and december_generator2026.xlsx answered 301 (not yet published).

records_total is the Operating sheet (28,485 rows); records_for_country is fossil+nuclear operating generators (3,144 plants). Planned sheet: 2,359 rows, 523 fossil/nuclear (5 nuclear); Retired: 7,322 rows, 5,287 fossil/nuclear.

sources.name: Form EIA-923 detailed data (Power Plant Operations Report), 2025 final
sources.format: Zip of Excel (.xlsx) workbooks: Schedules 2-5 (Pages 1-7), Schedules 6-7, Schedule 8
sources.summary: EIA-923 gives 2025 net generation in MWh and fuel use by plant, prime mover and fuel, nuclear by reactor unit; it joins EIA-860 on plant code. Vogtle's four reactors summed 37.1 million MWh.
sources.coverage_note: Final 2025 data (released 2026-09-14); plant x fuel level, generator level only on Page 4.
caveats: Net generation only; no gross column seen.
3,025 of 3,128 fossil/nuclear plants of EIA-860 appear in Page 1.

problems: records_total is Page 1 rows (plant x prime mover x fuel); records_for_country is the number of EIA-860 fossil/nuclear plants present in Page 1 (of 3,128).
The year-to-date 2026 file f923_2026.zip was listed on the page but not downloaded.

example.example_request: curl -L -o f923_2025.zip https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia923/xls/f923_2025.zip && unzip f923_2025.zip -d eia923_2025  # EIA923_Schedules_2_3_4_5_M_12_2025_Final.xlsx, sheet 'Page 1 Generation and Fuel Data' (header row 6), filter Plant Id = 649
example.example_result: Plant Id 649 Vogtle, operator Georgia Power Co: Net Generation 2025 by Nuclear Unit Id 1/2/3/4 = 10,205,689 / 9,489,888 / 9,616,946 / 7,831,892 MWh (sum 37,144,415).

local_terms.meaning: EIA's plant identifier, same across EIA-860, 860M and 923.
Nameplate is the generator rating; net summer/winter are net capacities in those seasons.
Machine type driving the generator (ST steam turbine, GT gas turbine, CC combined cycle...).
Company responsible for day-to-day operations, i.e. the operator, not necessarily the owner.

provenance.note: Minutes are researcher estimates. Counts describe documented passes, not publication approval. Missing history or effort is not reconstructed.
